public_rationale: The claim has two parts. The second part, that hallucination has no principled fix, fits a September 2025 OpenAI paper saying hallucinations persist even in state-of-the-art systems. The main part says reliable agents cannot be built unless hallucination is solved. That is a necessity claim. It could only be refuted by agents widely accepted as reliable while their models still hallucinate, and no agreed threshold for 'reliable' exists. The evidence I found is consistent with the claim but does not test it. So I leave it unresolved.
limitations: Causal necessity claims are hard to test.
